title: Offline handling and reconnect behavior
description: Project: Offline handling and reconnect behavior. Build and understand this project with step-by-step guidance.

data.text: Users will lose connectivity. They will walk into an elevator, board a subway, or open the app on an airplane. An offline-capable communication platform does not just queue messages; it reconciles state, handles conflicts, and resumes seamlessly when connectivity returns. This lesson covers the patterns that make offline behavior feel like an edge case rather than a crash.

items: Detect offline state using the browser navigator.onLine API combined with WebSocket close events
Queue outbound messages in IndexedDB or localStorage while the connection is down
Flush the queue on reconnect in the order messages were created, not the order they were queued by retry timers
Handle message deduplication on the server using idempotency keys so retried messages do not create duplicates
Show an offline indicator in the UI only after confirming the transport is unavailable, not just on navigator.onLine
Handle the long tail of slow networks: timeouts should be generous on initial connection but aggressive on retries
Reconcile local state with server state after reconnect to avoid showing stale data as current

terms.definition: Storing outgoing operations in a local outbox before attempting to send them, ensuring no message is lost during disconnection.
A low-level browser API for storing significant amounts of structured data, including files and blobs, with transaction support.
A unique identifier generated by the client for each message, allowing the server to safely process retries without creating duplicates.
The process of comparing local state with server state after a disruption and merging changes without data loss.
A browser API that provides information about the user's network connection, including effective type and round-trip time estimates.

data.text: Users judge the quality of a communication platform by what happens when they lose connectivity. If the app crashes, loses messages, or shows stale data after reconnect, trust erodes quickly. Senior engineers design the offline experience intentionally: they show clear status, queue work safely, and reconcile state deterministically so the app recovers as if nothing happened.

data.title: Test offline behavior before launch
data.text: Use Chrome DevTools Network tab to simulate offline and slow-3G conditions. Use the Application tab to inspect IndexedDB entries while offline. Do not rely on airplane mode alone because OS-level behavior varies by platform and browser.

items: Listen to window online and offline events as a primary signal
Treat WebSocket close with code 1006 as a secondary offline signal
Start the outbox queue immediately when either signal indicates unavailability
Assign a client-generated UUID to every queued message before storing it
Store messages with createdAt, idempotencyKey, payload, and retryCount
On reconnect, sort the queue by createdAt and send in order, not by insertion order if retries reordered them
Remove messages from the queue only after receiving a server acknowledgment

data.caption: Offline queue and reconnect reconciliation flow
data.definition:
graph TD
    A[User sends message] --> B{Online?}
    B -->|Yes| C[Send via WebSocket]
    B -->|No| D[Store in IndexedDB outbox]
    D --> E[Show queued indicator]
    C --> F{Server ACK?}
    F -->|Yes| G[Confirm in UI]
    F -->|No| D
    H[Network restored] --> I[Flush outbox in order]
    I --> J[Server processes with idempotency key]
    J --> K[Remove from outbox]
    K --> L[Sync missed messages]
    L --> M[Reconcile local state]

items: Last-write-wins: use server-assigned timestamps and overwrite local state with newer server state
Operational transforms: not necessary for simple chat; use only for collaborative editing
Vector clocks: complex but precise; use when multiple users can edit the same message
Merge on reconnect: download all messages created since the last sync and insert missing ones by ID

data.title: Implement an offline message outbox
data.description: Build an outbox pattern that queues messages in IndexedDB while offline, flushes them in order on reconnect, and handles idempotent server acknowledgment.
steps: Create an IndexedDB database with an outbox object store keyed by client-generated UUID
Implement a queue manager that intercepts send calls when the socket is disconnected
On reconnect, read all outbox entries sorted by createdAt
Send each message with its idempotency key and remove it only after server ACK
Show the user a badge with the number of queued messages
Handle the edge case where a message was sent but the ACK was lost: deduplicate on the server
data.expectedOutcome: You should be able to write messages while offline, see them queue visually, and have them appear in the conversation after reconnect without duplicates.

items.question: Should I show an offline banner immediately?
items.answer: Wait until the WebSocket close event confirms the transport is down. navigator.onLine can be true while the WebSocket is broken, and showing a banner too early creates false alarms.

items.question: How big should the outbox queue be?
items.answer: Set a reasonable limit, such as five hundred messages. If the user exceeds it, show a warning and offer to archive older drafts. Unbounded queues can exhaust storage on low-end devices.

items.question: What if the server receives messages out of order?
items.answer: The server should reorder by client-assigned createdAt or a server-assigned sequence number. If the gap is too large, request a full sync from the client.

data.title: Summary
points: Detect offline using both browser events and WebSocket close codes
Queue messages in IndexedDB with idempotency keys
Flush in order on reconnect and reconcile state with the server
Use last-write-wins for simple chat, operational transforms only for collaborative editing
data.takeaway: Offline handling is a first-class feature, not a nice-to-have. Users should be able to read and write even when the network is gone.
